claims.statement: dcode headless-resume integration tests use isolated subprocess profiles because profile paths and the sessions database are captured at import; they validate persisted-thread resume behavior through the real CLI and server boundary without using a developer profile.

dcode passes shared ServerConfig data to its LangGraph subprocess through DEEPAGENTS_CODE_SERVER-prefixed environment variables, scaffolds a temporary runtime, waits for the agent graph, binds the RemoteAgent workspace, and reaps an unhanded-off server even on cancellation or readiness failure.

The dcode Makefile is the package test-command authority: its unit target defaults to `tests/unit_tests/`, runs in parallel with socket access disabled except Unix sockets, accepts `PYTEST_EXTRA`, and its integration target selects `tests/integration_tests/` with a 30-second timeout.

dcode unit-test collection creates a synthetic DEEPAGENTS_HOME before package imports and uses autouse fixtures to restore environment and selected process-global runtime state, preventing developer configuration and tracing state from leaking between tests.

The checkpointer compatibility patch forwards delta-channel history through the private LangGraph API adapter only when its inner saver overrides the base method, otherwise retaining the base ancestor walk; tests seed SQLite graph history to verify both paths return equivalent data.

The LangSmith runtime override runs only untraced traceable setup/end bookkeeping inline, retaining LangSmith's default thread hop for other calls; focused tests verify untraced success and errors avoid executor work while traced nested runs retain their hierarchy.

The in-memory run-queue patch wakes a waiting scheduler after Runs.put while leaving upstream run claiming and fallback polling intact; it is idempotent and declines to patch unexpected private API shapes.

dcode fences checkpoint mutations with a per-thread ownership token and client reservation: stale, released, crashed, or superseded clients cannot write, and the owned SQLite saver applies the guard to checkpoint writes and pending writes.

LocalContextMiddleware keeps its snapshot, fingerprint, and refresh cutoff in private state, refreshes context after a valid summarization cutoff without replacing the original snapshot, and reuses a parent snapshot for same-thread forked subagents.

ManagedMemoryGuardMiddleware restores altered marker-delimited onboarding memory while preserving unrelated edits, returns an error for the guarded mutation, and rejects deletion of managed or unreadable guarded files before the tool runs.

dcode virtualizes chat transcripts by retaining lightweight message data while mounting a bounded widget window; spacer height estimates and protection of streaming or live rows preserve scroll geometry and prevent unsafe pruning.

Transcript hydration is driven by actual chat vertical-offset changes, covering wheel, keyboard, and scrollbar interactions; Textual pilot tests prove archived history hydrates from both transcript edges.

Autocomplete tests protect deterministic fuzzy ranking against a reference scorer, isolate durable thread-reference completion as an @@ grammar that inserts canonical thread tokens, and reject unsafe filenames from suggestions and input.

Headless dcode tests verify that non-interactive startup passes `interactive=False`, skill trust interrupts resume with explicit denial, and project hooks remain unavailable unless the headless invocation explicitly opts in.

Configuration tests enforce that project dotenv values cannot influence interpolation in the trusted global dotenv or set user-level trust and approval controls, while trusted global dotenv values may set those controls.

MCP trust tests prevent untrusted project remote servers from reaching the loader, admit a remote server only when whole-project trust is explicit, and ensure disabled servers are removed even from a trusted configuration.

Plugin update tests protect the lifecycle in which a discovered version is persisted and announced once without installation, refresh failure retains the saved availability, manifest auto-update installs the new version, and an explicit CLI update clears the available record.

FinalMarkdown pilot tests ensure finished replies preserve the streamed Markdown rows across widths and themes, route an encoded link target unchanged through the checked opener, and preserve wide code and selection text at narrow widths.

Harbor LangGraph adapter tests verify that the dcode graph runs as a local headless auto-approved agent, derives a safe assistant identifier, and removes provider and tracing credentials from the shell backend environment without mutating the outer process environment.
ModalSandbox batch transfer tests require a per-file response and continuation after file-open errors, preserving successful binary transfer and closing each handle.

Workflow secret-scoping tests statically parse GitHub workflows to require package-scoped integration secret expressions and an OpenWiki job with read-only workflow permissions, a dedicated environment, credential-free checkout, and a later write-capable app token.

The eval experiment-name tests preserve historical name derivation, sanitize branch and model delimiters, omit empty optional category and reasoning segments, and verify the CLI reads its GitHub and Harbor inputs from the environment.

The evals and Modal Makefiles keep package-local test routing distinct: evals unit tests disable network sockets and model-backed evals require `MODEL`, while Modal has separate socket-disabled unit and 30-second integration targets.
